claims.content: Customer
The Customer initiates the use case by clicking the 'Go' button or the 'Find Product' button to execute a product search.

After a successful search, the system displays a search-results table whose columns, in default order, are: Action (checkbox), item thumbnail image, Product ID (SKU #) with link to SKU History page, Auction ID number, Description, Opening Bid, High Bid, Item Unit Cost, Start time (initially blank), End time (initially blank), Duration (initially blank), Product Type (e.g., Ring, Single Stone), and Increment.

After a successful search, the displayed search results include thumbnail images of products, support sorting by clicking underlined column headers, and can be further refined using autofilter functions similar to Excel.

After a successful Product ID search, the system displays a 'Search Results for Item' section containing a table with columns for Auction Status, Auction_Seq, Start Date/Time, End Date/Time, Reserve, High Bid, # of Bids, and Winner / High Bidder, populated with rows corresponding to the matching auction history.
Products must be marked as both 'Auction Available' and 'Auction Eligible' in the JTV enterprise systems to be counted in inventory numbers.
The system has inventory data populated and available for the Customer to access.
The Customer wants to browse and search auction inventory to find products that meet their selected filtering and search criteria.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The Customer wants to browse and search auction inventory to find products that meet their selected filtering and search criteria.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The Customer applies one or more browse/search filters or parameters to the auction inventory and receives a display of the matching product(s).
scope_contract.start_boundary: The Customer has selected or entered search/filter criteria and is ready to browse/search the auction inventory.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The Customer has successfully found and viewed the auction inventory items matching the applied filters/search parameters.
in_scope_actions: Filtering by selectable categories such as Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, and Location
Searching by configurable parameters such as Product ID, Customer Email Address, Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, Product Type, and Cost Range
Combining search parameters to filter results
variant_dimensions: Selectable browse categories/filters: Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, Location
Configurable search parameters: Product ID, Customer Email Address, Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, Product Type, Cost Range

claims.content: If a search returns no matching products, the system displays a 'No Results Found' page that includes: (1) an apology/message stating no matches were found, (2) a 'Search Tips' section with five suggestions (check typos, remove unnecessary words, try plural/singular forms, use fewer/generic keywords, contact support), and (3) a 'May We Suggest'/'Popular Searches' section with static lists of popular gemstone and jewelry searches plus dynamically updated search terms/phrases using Omniture data. The exception branch outcome is the display of this No Results Found page.
If the Customer clicks a link that contains no product (which routinely happens for collectibles), the system serves a 'No Results Found' page. The exception branch outcome is this no-results page.

If all items matching the Customer's criteria lack an available product image, those items are prevented from appearing in search results; this hard filter may result in an empty or incomplete result set despite the other search/filter criteria matching.

If the Customer is not signed in when clicking anywhere within a product module (except the QuickBid button), the system presents the sign-in page; after the Customer completes sign-in, the system delivers the Customer to the Product Details page.

missing_aspects: Recovery/continuation after the 'No Results Found' page display is not documented; the evidence specifies the page display as the branch outcome.
Precise main-flow step numbers for exception divergence points are not available in the provided context.

claims.content: The Customer browses the auction inventory using the Endeca or Endeca-like search and navigation capability.

The Customer specifies one or more criteria by selecting browse filters from scrolling list boxes (e.g., Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Material Purity, Brand, Location, with multi-select via the Control key) and/or entering search parameters (e.g., Product ID, Customer Email Address, Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, Product Type, Cost Range, optionally using wildcards for Product ID and low/high cost values for Cost Range); multiple filters and parameters may be combined.
The Customer clicks the 'Go' or 'Find Product' button to execute the search.

When the Customer searches by Product ID, the system displays a 'Search Results for Item' section containing a table with columns for Auction Status, Auction_Seq, Start Date/Time, End Date/Time, Reserve, High Bid, # of Bids, and Winner / High Bidder, populated with rows corresponding to the matching auction history. For searches using other criteria, the system displays a table titled 'Search Results' containing columns for Action, Image, Product ID, Auction #, Description, Open Bid, High Bid, Unit Cost, Starts, Ends, Duration, Product Type, and Increment, with rows showing the matching auction items.
The displayed Search Results include thumbnail images, can be sorted by clicking underlined column headers, and can be further refined using autofilter functions similar to Excel.

Diverges from Step 1: Instead of starting with Endeca navigation, the Customer may access the browse/search capability via the Site Map page, which lists all available Categories (Jewelry, Gemstones, Collectibles, Watches), Product Types (e.g., Rings, Necklaces, Bracelets), and Gemstone Types (e.g., Tanzanite, Diamond, Ruby) as direct links to specific pages or Endeca results pages.

Diverges from Step 1: Instead of starting with Endeca navigation, the Customer may enter product browsing via SEO-optimized landing pages focused on specific gemstone types (e.g., 'tanzanite page') or product types (e.g., 'Rings page'), which contain direct links to relevant product categories such as 'all loose tanzanite stones' or 'all tanzanite rings'.

Diverges from Step 2: The Customer may choose between 'Items currently online only' or 'All sellable auction inventory' via radio buttons; this selection does not impact the results of the 'Red status' columns.

Diverges from Step 2: The Customer may refine the result-set composition by enabling or disabling viewing items with or without images, or with or without a valid (sellable) location, via radio buttons; these options are combinable filter options.

Diverges from Step 2: The Customer may group the results using a scrolling list box with options including Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material, Material Purity, Product Group, Brand, Inventory Realm (Red, White), Inventory Aging Bucket, J/G Score, and Ring Size; the selected grouping option generates corresponding columns in the Results section.
Diverges from Step 5: The Customer may switch the displayed product results between 'List View' and 'Catalog View'.
Diverges from Step 5: The Customer may sort the product results by 'Current Price: low to high' using a dropdown menu.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_postconditions_reachability] Postcondition 3 requires a 'Search Results for Item' table with auction-history columns after a Product ID search, but the Main Flow always displays a generic 'Search Results' table (step 4) and does not include a Product ID-search branch to the 'Search Results for Item' state. Thus the Main Flow cannot lead to this postcondition. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit evidence that the 'Search Results for Item' section is located on the SKU History page))

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] The Trigger is the click on Go/Find Product to execute a search, but Main Flow step 1 describes browsing inventory and step 2 describes specifying criteria before step 3 repeats the same click. The main flow therefore does not continue from the Trigger; it restarts before the triggering event, creating a temporal gap/contradiction. (still no supporting evidence after retrieval)

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] The Trigger is defined as the Customer clicking the 'Go' or 'Find Product' button to execute a search, but the Main Flow places that same click as step 3 after steps 1 and 2 where the Customer browses the inventory and specifies criteria. Therefore the use case cannot start with that Trigger and then continue into the Main Flow; the Trigger duplicates a later main-flow step and precedes the browse/criteria actions that must happen before the click.

[altflow_diverge_points] Alternative flow claim at index 4 says 'Diverges from Step 2' but describes grouping the results using a scrolling list box and generating corresponding columns in the Results section. Main flow Step 2 is specifically about specifying search/filter criteria; grouping results is a results-display/presentation behavior, not a criteria-specification behavior, so Step 2 is not a logically related divergence point.

inconsistency_hints: The Trigger states the use case starts when the Customer clicks Go/Find Product after already entering criteria. However, Main Flow steps 1-2 have the Customer browsing and specifying criteria before that click, placing those steps before the Trigger and creating a discontinuity/restart instead of continuing from it.

Postcondition 2 describes a filtered product list made of Product Modules, but the Main Flow only ends with a tabular Search Results view (steps 4-5). No Main Flow step or branch produces the Product Module display, so the postcondition is not reachable from the flow.

Postcondition 3 requires that a successful Product ID search displays a 'Search Results for Item' section with an auction-history table, but Main Flow step 4 only specifies the generic 'Search Results' table and no branch/step covers the Product ID search result view. Therefore the postcondition is not reachable from the described main flow.
